source_text: Ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τῶν ἀνόμων ὑπερμάχων τῆς εἰδωλολατρίας προστάγματα ἀσεβῆ κατὰ τῶν εὐσεβούντων Χριστιανῶν κατὰ πόλιν καὶ χώραν ἐξετίθετο, ὥστε αὐτοὺς ἀναγκάζεσθαι σπένδειν τοῖς ματαίοις εἰδώλοις. Συλληφθέντες οὖν οἱ ἅγιοι ἄνδρες εἰσήχθησαν πρὸς τὸν τῆς Ῥώμης ἔπαρχον ὀνόματι Ῥουστικόν.
orientation: The narrator opens the account as orders go out against the Christians and the holy men are arrested and brought to Rusticus the prefect of Rome.
pass_a_gloss: In the time of the lawless champions of idolatry, impious orders against the Christians practicing true worship were being set forth city by city and district by district, so that they were being compelled to pour a drink-offering to the vain idols. Therefore, after being arrested, the holy men were led in to the prefect of Rome, by name Rusticus.

choices.why: Keeps brief glossary English for both terms and preserves participle force against impious orders.
Uses glossary idol and keeps mataios as empty contempt, not a doctrinal false-god claim.
Literal libation act compelled by the orders, distinct from general sacrifice verb thuo.
Keeps military-partisan force of hypermachos rather than neutral support.

pass_b_english: In the time of the lawless champions of idolatry, impious orders against the Christians practicing true worship were posted in every city and countryside. They compelled them to pour a drink-offering to the vain idols.
After their arrest, the holy men were brought before Rusticus, the prefect of Rome.
